references.text: Samson tells Delilah that he will become weak like an ordinary man if bound with seven fresh bowstrings—this is the first of his false answers about the secret behind his strength.
The first time Delilah tries to bind Samson and cries out that the Philistines are coming, but he breaks the bonds—the same pattern is repeated here in verse 12.
Samson gives Delilah the second false answer, saying that new, unused ropes will make him weak—this is the background for the action in verse 12.
The third attempt to bind Samson follows the same pattern: Delilah binds him and cries out about the Philistines.
Earlier, Samson was bound with new ropes by the men of Judah, but the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he snapped the bonds like burnt thread.
Finally, the Lord's strength leaves Samson after he reveals his true secret—in contrast to verse 12, where he still has his strength.
